findings.highlight: Transformation of the skin, necrosis of the tips of the limbs… I hear there were even students on the verge of blindness.
findings.evidenceJa: 一生残る傷を負った者もいた
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese says only that some students suffered lifelong injuries; the detailed list is inactive source text.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores deleted medical details, adding specific skin changes, necrosis, and near-blindness to the public aftermath.

findings.highlight: not the type to stop when he’s beaten
findings.evidenceJa: やられっ放しで黙ってるタイプじゃない
findings.governingReading: Shinji is not the type to take a beating and remain silent.
findings.explanation: Stop changes his refusal to let humiliation pass unanswered into generic persistence.

findings.highlight: He’s the kind of guy that’ll take revenge.
findings.evidenceJa: 殴られたら倍にして返す性格だ
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese ends after saying Shinji will not remain silent; the line that he pays back a blow double is commented out.
findings.explanation: The English restores deleted characterization and simplifies its doubled retaliation into generic revenge.

findings.highlight: It’s “Hey now. It’s not like I’m not thinking
findings.evidenceJa: 驚いた。やりますね、シロウ
findings.governingReading: Saber praises Shirou’s thinking, and he answers that he is not acting without thought.
findings.explanation: Stray It’s and an opening quotation corrupt the beginning of Shirou’s reply.

findings.highlight: the kind of guy that would be resting at home
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の家に潜伏するほど落ち着いた男
findings.governingReading: Shirou judges Shinji too agitated to lie low in his own house.
findings.explanation: Resting removes concealment and turns a judgment about Shinji’s agitated temperament into ordinary inactivity.

findings.highlight: it is for Sakura’s best as well
findings.evidenceJa: 桜にとっても最善の方法
findings.governingReading: Shirou tells himself that staying away is also the best course for Sakura.
findings.explanation: For Sakura’s best is unidiomatic and blurs the self-justifying conclusion.

findings.highlight: there’s no findings yet
findings.evidenceJa: コレといった手応えはない
findings.governingReading: Their sweep of the larger buildings has produced no promising response or lead.
findings.explanation: The number disagreement is grammatically conspicuous, and findings sounds like a report rather than a felt magical lead.

findings.highlight: I stand still for a while
findings.evidenceJa: 少しだけ立ち止まって
findings.governingReading: Shirou stops only briefly to take a deep breath and steady his breathing.
findings.explanation: For a while lengthens the pause and weakens how determinedly he pushes through his injury.

findings.highlight: is there something wron
findings.evidenceJa: 何か異状でもあり
findings.governingReading: Saber begins asking whether something is wrong before her expression stiffens.
findings.explanation: The English visibly truncates wrong and its closing punctuation.

findings.highlight: I hold my face with one hand
findings.evidenceJa: 片手で頭を押さえる
findings.governingReading: Shirou presses one hand to his head as dizziness and exhaustion overtake him.
findings.explanation: Face moves the gesture to a different body part.

findings.highlight: I could touch her shoulder if I leaned over a bit
findings.evidenceJa: 肩が触れるほどの近さ
findings.governingReading: They sit close enough that leaning slightly would make their shoulders touch.
findings.explanation: The English turns reciprocal accidental proximity into Shirou deliberately touching Saber’s shoulder.

findings.highlight: Heyno, hold on Saber
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっいや、待てってセイバー
findings.governingReading: Shirou stammers for Saber to wait.
findings.explanation: Hey and no are fused, corrupting the flustered interruption.

findings.highlight: I don’t know what kind of a guy would be able to calm down
findings.evidenceJa: 男としてどうかと思う
findings.governingReading: Shirou jokes that a man able to stay calm with a beautiful girl this close would be questionable as a man.
findings.explanation: The English turns his pointed, self-conscious standard of masculinity into a vague question about what kind of man could remain calm.

findings.highlight: it seems you should lie down
findings.evidenceJa: 横になった方がいいのでしょうか
findings.governingReading: Saber tentatively wonders whether Shirou ought to lie down.
findings.explanation: The English turns her uncertain, exploratory question into an assertion.

findings.highlight: All I have to do now is to keep on breathing deeply and
findings.evidenceJa: 懸命に深呼吸を繰り返して
findings.governingReading: Shirou desperately repeats deep breaths while trying not to remain conscious of Saber beside him.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the sentence hanging on and without a completion.

findings.highlight: the blackened woods
findings.evidenceJa: 黒こげになった材木
findings.governingReading: Charred timbers smolder across the burned field.
findings.explanation: Woods changes pieces of burned lumber and structural remains into a forested area.

findings.highlight: sounds like a small firework
findings.evidenceJa: 線香花火の音
findings.governingReading: The faint crackling of the timbers reminds Shirou of a sparkler.
findings.explanation: Small firework loses the specific quiet, dying crackle of a senko hanabi.

findings.highlight: There are only burned corpses
findings.evidenceJa: 焼け焦げた残骸
findings.governingReading: Burned wreckage surrounds Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English inserts burned corpses before restarting the sentence, adding bodies absent from this line.

findings.highlight: There are only burned corpses There is only burnt wreckage around me
findings.evidenceJa: まわりには焼け焦げた残骸
findings.governingReading: One statement establishes the burned wreckage around Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English prints two competing versions back to back.

findings.highlight: I have burns all over my body
findings.evidenceJa: 肌はところどころが火傷していて
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s skin is burned in places.
findings.explanation: All over exaggerates localized burns into whole-body coverage.

findings.highlight: there’s a bad burn across my chest
findings.evidenceJa: 胸には一際鋭い、熱い感触
findings.governingReading: His chest carries an especially sharp, hot sensation.
findings.explanation: The English converts a felt, unusually acute sensation into an asserted burn and spreads it across the chest.

findings.highlight: I feel like I could grab my heart if I put my fingers into the inflamed chest. innards with my fingers.
findings.evidenceJa: じかに中身を掴めそう
findings.governingReading: His chest is gouged open so deeply that touching it feels as though he could directly grasp what is inside.
findings.explanation: The English specifies his heart, adds an inflamed chest, and appends a second fragment about innards, corrupting the image and sentence.

findings.highlight: I was manly and did not panic
findings.evidenceJa: 潔く、取り乱す事もなかった
findings.governingReading: Shirou accepts the inevitability cleanly and does not lose control.
findings.explanation: Manly replaces composed resignation with an unsupported gender judgment.

findings.highlight: watched myself as I grew thinner
findings.evidenceJa: 薄れていく自分を眺める
findings.governingReading: He watches his own consciousness or existence fade.
findings.explanation: Grew thinner literalizes 薄れる as bodily thinness and obscures his approach to death.

findings.highlight: I thought to seek help as long as I was alive and I reached out my hands
findings.evidenceJa: 助けを求めようと思って
findings.governingReading: Even in fading consciousness, Shirou thinks he should keep seeking help until the end.
findings.explanation: The English adds the completed physical act of reaching out his hands, which the source does not state here.

findings.highlight: I wake up suddenly
findings.evidenceJa: 勢いよく体を起こす
findings.governingReading: Shirou bolts his body upright and opens his shirt to inspect himself.
findings.explanation: Wake up replaces the visible bodily action and prematurely resolves the uncertain boundary between dream and recollection.

findings.highlight: Saber is right next to me and answers as if nothing has happened.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーはすぐ側にいて、何事もなかったように返答をした
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese ends with Saber noting that Shirou looks better; the narration about her remaining beside him is commented out.
findings.explanation: The English restores deleted narration and adds a pointed appearance of nonchalance.

findings.highlight: Even if it was bad for me
findings.evidenceJa: 居眠りした俺が悪いにしても
findings.governingReading: Shirou concedes that dozing off was his own fault.
findings.explanation: The English instead suggests the sleep itself was bad for him, losing his admission of responsibility.

findings.highlight: that’s only in hindsight opinion
findings.evidenceJa: そりゃ結果論だ
findings.governingReading: Shirou objects that Saber can say that only in hindsight.
findings.explanation: In hindsight opinion is malformed English.

findings.highlight: she’s right in this case
findings.evidenceJa: 今回はセイバーの言い分のが正しい
findings.governingReading: Page 61 is entirely commented out in the active Japanese.
findings.explanation: The English restores deleted narration in which Shirou explicitly concedes that Saber is right.

findings.highlight: became his foster child
findings.evidenceJa: そのまま養子になった
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu saves Shirou and formally adopts him.
findings.explanation: Foster child substitutes a different family and legal relationship for adoption.

findings.highlight: The one person who survived it
findings.evidenceJa: そこで生き残った俺
findings.governingReading: Shirou describes himself as someone who survived at the war’s final site.
findings.explanation: The one person asserts that he was the sole survivor, which this line does not establish.

findings.highlight: Ehwell, that’s
findings.evidenceJa: えいや、それは
findings.governingReading: Shirou stumbles as he begins to answer Saber.
findings.explanation: Eh and well are fused into a typographical corruption.

findings.highlight: SoEmiya Shirou
findings.evidenceJa: だから衛宮士郎は
findings.governingReading: Shirou concludes that Emiya Shirou must bear responsibility.
findings.explanation: So and Emiya are fused, damaging a central statement of his survivor guilt.

findings.highlight: If I want retribution for those that died
findings.evidenceJa: 死んでいった人たちに報いたいなら
findings.governingReading: Shirou says that if he wants to repay or honor the dead, he should prevent future disasters.
findings.explanation: Retribution introduces vengeance or punishment into an ethic of answering the dead through prevention.

findings.highlight: I don’t remember the details
findings.evidenceJa: そんな細かいコトまで覚えてない
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese proceeds from Saber recalling Shirou’s priority statement to her diagnosis of him; Shirou’s aside is commented out.
findings.explanation: The English restores deleted interior narration that makes him dismiss the remembered wording as a minor detail.

findings.highlight: I became confident about it then
findings.evidenceJa: その時に確信した
findings.governingReading: Saber says that at that moment she became certain Shirou had no intention of saving himself.
findings.explanation: Became confident is unidiomatic here and weakens certainty into increased confidence.

findings.highlight: As if… …Even stating that fact is a crime
findings.evidenceJa: それが罪だと言うかのように
findings.governingReading: Saber declares his lack of self-preservation while looking at him as though that condition were a fault or sin.
findings.explanation: The English attaches criminality to stating the fact, reversing what her gaze condemns.

findings.highlight: We are certainly putting a burden on you by being here
findings.evidenceJa: ここにいては貴方に負担をかける
findings.governingReading: Saber acknowledges that remaining in this place burdens Shirou.
findings.explanation: We makes Saber and Shirou jointly cause the burden rather than locating it in the traumatic place.

findings.highlight: It can’t be true, butfor some reason
findings.evidenceJa: ある筈がないのに、なぜか
findings.governingReading: Shirou insists it cannot be true, yet cannot find a single word of denial.
findings.explanation: But and for are fused at the hinge of the contradiction.
